dir:medium.en: 1914 lithographic poster + woodcut/linocut + old satirical war maps: thick outline, 3–4 flat colours, paper grain. Background — muted earth tones; each faction gets one sharp accent.

dir:not_tc.en: Difference from Trench Crusade: no oil painting, stained glass, halos, saints, Gothic cathedral forms or detailed body horror — our tone is mythological folk art (bronze ornament, folk textiles, towers), and the horror is implied.

fvis:colchis:materials.en: bronze, marsh wood, leather, wax-soaked canvas

fvis:colchis:silhouette.en: horned helmets, round bronze shields, ox-shaped machines, houses on stilts

fvis:colchis:avoid.en: copying the Greek hoplite; religious ornament

fvis:iberia:materials.en: mail shirt, iron, felt, stone, copper coils

fvis:iberia:silhouette.en: mail coif, small round shield, lightning coils on the back, nagazi dogs, tower-shaped tanks

fvis:iberia:avoid.en: Khevsur cross ornament (religious association); grey military tunic with armband (fascist association) — uniform: chokha, felt cloak, felt, mail shirt

fvis:hell:materials.en: black lacquered steel, ash-coloured canvas, glass gas masks

fvis:hell:silhouette.en: strict rectangular shapes, identical ranks, high collars, geometric rank badges

fvis:hell:emblem.en: our own geometric rank badges (not grimoire seals)

fvis:hell:avoid.en: flies, plague, the seven sins (TC); real sigils; religious iconography

fvis:harness:materials.en: chains, wooden yokes, stitched cloth, rusted iron

fvis:harness:silhouette.en: asymmetric, ragged; chains and yokes on the body; wheeled wagons; devis in harness

fvis:harness:emblem.en: a broken chain beneath a yoke

fvis:harness:avoid.en: the uniform or symbol of any real nation (the heretics come from every nation)

fvis:listeners:materials.en: masks, wax, bronze listening horns, locks and keys

fvis:listeners:silhouette.en: ear horns on the helmet, faceless masks, cloaks, strings of locks on the back

fvis:listeners:emblem.en: a closed ear with a padlock

fvis:ottoman:materials.en: stone, wood (oriel windows), bazaar cloth, copper pumps

fvis:ottoman:silhouette.en: city craftsmen and firefighters (tulumbacı), mehter drums, Karagöz shadows

fvis:ottoman:emblem.en: our own: a bazaar gate and a pump

tc:khalkotavri.en: TC has the "Brazen Bull" — the Iron Sultanate's living siege engine with a fire cannon. Our Khalkotavri comes from the myth of the Golden Fleece: a four-legged ox breathing fire from its mouth, with Colchian geometric ornament, a herder in front striking it with a staff. No cannon on its back, no Eastern/Ottoman style, green patina.

tc:janissaries.en: In TC the "Janissaries" are Iron Sultanate infantry (55 ducats). Ours are volunteer soldiers from the city guilds: bazaar cloth, a pump hose, a firefighter's helmet — not the sultan's guard, not the white börk.

tc:sipahis.en: TC has a "Sipahi automaton cavalry" (a variant). Our Sipahis are living riders on living horses, with no automatons.

tc:byzantium_grotesque.en: In TC the "Lions of Jabir" are alchemical creatures. Our Lion of the Magnaura is a steam version of the historical throne automaton (10th c., Liudprand): gold plate, a mechanical roar, a ceremonial form.

tc:yoke_slaves.en: TC has "Yoke Fiends". In the English version the name must change (e.g. Harness-bound); visual: a group of people chained to one beam, not a demon.

tc:automaton_phalanx.en: Automatons exist in TC too (the Sipahi). Our phalanx draws on the Greek bronze Talos motif — a wall of shields, not cavalry.
